note: Every third-party MCP server this plugin ships a row for. `mcp/shim.mjs` reads this file to pick a local copy or fall back to a package runner; `scripts/fetch-mcp.mjs` fills `.mcp-vendor/` from it. Versions are pinned here on purpose: an MCP server's tool vocabulary is part of this plugin's contract, so it must not drift under us between sessions. Vendor kinds: `npm` (registry tarball, exact version), `github` (git spec pinned to a commit sha — for upstreams that publish nowhere else, e.g. mcp-svd is absent from the npm registry), `pypi` (venv, exact version; run via `-m <module>` or a console `script`).

servers.summary: draw.io diagram generation (official jgraph MCP): Mermaid / XML / CSV in, editable .drawio out
Deterministic calculator: arithmetic, unit conversion, date and calendar arithmetic
ARM CMSIS-SVD register-map lookup: peripherals, registers, bit-fields, addresses (upstream mcp-svd)
upstreamNotes: GitHub-only: the npm registry has no `mcp-svd` package (404), so this is the one row that pins a commit sha instead of a released version. There are no tags to pin to, and the repository is a single-author project created 2026-03-10 with one star — read it before you rely on it.

No `prepare` script, by design: the author's last commit removed it so that installing from GitHub cannot execute `tsc` on the installer's machine, and committed the built `dist/` instead. That is why vendoring needs no build step, and why there is nothing to run at install time.
MIT is declared in package.json and in the directory listings, but the repository ships no LICENSE file. Recorded as declared-MIT, not verified-MIT.
Runtime dependencies are real and must be installed: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, express, fast-xml-parser. The committed dist/ is not self-contained — `node dist/index.js` fails on a bare checkout.

The npx fallback goes through npm's GitHub route, which downloads a codeload tarball and was then observed to stall indefinitely on the reference toolchain (no registry request, no error, >4 min, killed). Treat the fallback as the last resort it is: run `node scripts/fetch-mcp.mjs --only regmap` and use the vendored clone.

Every tool call takes an explicit `svd_file` path and there is no default. Bundled SVDs live at svd/STM32F411.svd, svd/nRF52840_xxAA.svd and svd/rp2040.svd relative to this row's vendor root; point it at your own chip's CMSIS-SVD for anything else. A chip that publishes no SVD cannot be served by this row at all.

servers.summary: KiCad schematic read-write and analysis (schematic sub-server of mcp-server-kicad)
servers.disabledReason: Opt-in, and deliberately NOT the pin tool family. This is schematic-capture plumbing: it reads and writes `.kicad_sch` files. It contains no pin-conflict or pin-assignment validator — that concept was searched for specifically and does not exist in its tool surface. Enable the row in cordis.patch.yml when a project actually has a KiCad schematic to work on.
prerequisites: KiCad 9.x or 10.x — only for ERC, DRC and the export tools (4 of the 42 schematic tools, which shell out to kicad-cli). The other 38 parse `.kicad_sch` directly and need no KiCad at all.

servers.disabledReason: Not vendorable and not enabled by default: upstream requires Python >=3.14 and a licensed Microsoft Visio install driven over COM, neither of which can be assumed on a contributor machine. Enable the row in cordis.patch.yml only where both hold.
